content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have developed a large program for a heating system and now I want to build a SCADA solution. Does anyone have any experience or advice? I think it's possible to do this in .NET, similar to a datalogger application. Any suggestions?

Hi, Creating an application to communicate directly with [product_name] PLCs can be challenging. You might want to look into drivers for [product_name] PLCs based on LabVIEW, or consider control panels designed for [product_name] and KNX integration. These references could inspire your approach. In my opinion, using a more advanced CPU type could be beneficial. Wishing you success! Best regards, [user_name]

Thanks [user_name], I see that it's preferable to develop on [version_no], but currently my system operates with [product_name] and works as intended. I’m not familiar with programming [version_no]. The SCADA is for my home, and I’m very satisfied with [product_name].

Hello [user_name], You can find an English version of an Excel-based [product_name] Data Logger at [url]. The original German version was created by [user_name] and is available at [url]. [user_name] enhanced it by adding a VBA-based visualization, which you can also find at [url]; this solution happens to be for a central heating system. It’s not a full SCADA solution, but it could help you get started and direct you toward further development. Even without speaking German, you can grasp the German version with online translation tools. Hope this helps!

Hi [user_name], thank you very much! This is ideal for my heating system. I don't speak German, but Visual Basic and Excel are sufficient for me. Thanks again. Once I've finished my project, I'll share updates here. Cheers to everyone!
Hello everyone. In the latest catalogue from [company_name] under Gateways and Interface Converters, there is an entry for KNX/[product_name] 7, but it requires using [version_no].

analysis.insight_summary: Users are exploring how to build a SCADA system for heating applications using existing [product_name] PLC setups. Although their current [product_name] PLC functions well, they find limited options for comprehensive SCADA integration and are pointed instead to Excel-based data loggers and suggestions to migrate to more advanced CPU platforms. Community-developed solutions are appreciated, but there is still a noticeable gap in integrated SCADA solutions for [product_name].
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope to build an accessible, interactive, and integrated SCADA system leveraging familiar technologies like .NET or Excel, favoring direct compatibility with their current [product_name] PLC infrastructure and seeking a straightforward development experience.
